headline: Tatum's 34 leads a record night from three in Charlotte

off.text: Next: Sun, Nov 8 vs Panthers, 1:00 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 8 vs Packers, 4:25 PM
Next: Sun, Nov 8 at Bucks, 8:00 PM

storylines: James Hagens, the NHL rookie points leader with 12, left Thursday's win after a cross-check to the lower back; an update is expected after Saturday's practice.
It opens a four-game homestand, part of a stretch of 10 home games in 11, and Boston has won three straight.
Florida plays in Washington on Saturday afternoon and is without Brad Marchand, who said he expects to be back in five or six weeks.
bruins.edge: Boston: it leads the Atlantic with 25 points to Florida's 20, and the Panthers are on the second night of a back-to-back.

storylines: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) are out; Henderson said Friday he was hospitalized for several days with unexplained neurological symptoms.
Hunter Henry (foot) returned to limited practice Friday and is one of seven Patriots listed as questionable.
Green Bay's Micah Parsons (knee) is out, and the Packers will start backups on the interior of their offensive line.
patriots.edge: Even on paper: both teams are 5–3, and each is missing a top player.

storylines: Boston beat Milwaukee 109–102 on Wednesday without Tatum, who rested that night and scored 34 in Charlotte on Friday.
The Bucks are 1–8, last in the East.
It's the second stop of a four-game trip that continues in Philadelphia on Tuesday and Toronto on Wednesday.
celtics.edge: Boston: it is 7–2 and won Wednesday's meeting, while Milwaukee has one win in nine games.

results.headline: Tatum's 34 leads a record night from three in Charlotte
results.takeaway: Jayson Tatum scored 18 of his 34 points in the first quarter and Boston made an NBA Cup-record 24 threes in a 119–80 rout. The Celtics are 2–0 in Cup play at plus-53 and have won seven of eight.

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: Tatum and Paul George opened with back-to-back threes, and Boston led 16–4 early. Tatum had 18 points with three threes, tying his career high for an opening quarter, and Boston went 9-of-17 from deep while Charlotte made 2 of 14.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: Boston led 53–25 with 6:34 left and 62–31 later in the quarter. Brandon Miller left with right groin soreness after scoring 8 on 3-of-10 shooting and did not return. The Celtics made 17 of 31 threes in the half, tying a franchise record, and Derrick White had all 18 of his points by the break.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Neemias Queta scored on a hook and a one-handed alley-oop from Tatum, and Jordan Walsh finished an and-one dunk off a Tatum pass. Tatum sat for good in the final minute of the quarter after 29 minutes.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Payton Pritchard hit threes in the fourth on the way to 12 points. Boston finished 24-of-44 from three; Charlotte shot 29.3% and lost its sixth straight.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: Back from a night of rest, he had 24 by halftime and a game-best plus-36 in 29 minutes.

performers.name: Derrick White
performers.note: Scored all 18 in the first half, 10 of them in the first quarter, as Boston pulled away.

performers.name: Payton Pritchard
performers.note: Cleared after Wednesday's eye abrasion, he hit threes in the first and fourth quarters off the bench.

results.oppLine: Naz Reid had 14 points on 6-of-17 shooting, Tidjane Salaun added 13 and Sion James 11 off the bench; Brandon Miller left in the second quarter.

celtics.headline: Celtics set NBA Cup record with 24 threes
celtics.summary: Boston went 24-of-44 from three in Friday's 119–80 win in Charlotte, an NBA Cup record. Its 17 threes in the first half tied a franchise record for a half.

celtics.headline: Boston 2–0 in Cup play at plus-53
celtics.summary: The Celtics have outscored their first two NBA Cup opponents by 53 points, and point differential is a group-play tiebreaker. They have two Cup games left and can still win East Group C or claim a wild card.

celtics.headline: Pritchard cleared, scores 12 off the bench
celtics.summary: Payton Pritchard was cleared to play after his right-eye abrasion and scored 12 points off the bench in Charlotte, including threes in the first and fourth quarters. Devin Carter (illness) was out.

celtics.headline: Tatum's 18 first-quarter points tie his career high
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 18 in the first quarter Friday, tying his career high for an opening quarter, and outscored Charlotte's starting five by himself. He finished with 34 points, a season-high five threes and 11-of-11 at the line in 29 minutes.

celtics.headline: Walsh starts as the lineup shuffle continues
celtics.summary: Jordan Walsh started Friday alongside Derrick White, Paul George, Tatum and Neemias Queta. Hugo Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman have also started at times, and Mitchell Robinson's run as a starter appears to be over.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: 'We need the best version' of George
celtics.summary: Paul George's 25 points against Milwaukee were his most since the season opener. "We need the best version of him for us to be a great team," Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Robinson's game still rounding into shape
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson is averaging 6.2 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3 fouls in 19.3 minutes, and Boston is minus-7.0 with him on the floor, compared with plus-8.1 with Neemias Queta. "I like where Mitch is at from a mentality standpoint," Joe Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Robinson sprains left thumb in Houston
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson briefly left Monday's game with a sprained left thumb and returned with his hand strapped. He finished with 4 points and 4 rebounds in 15:13, a minus-16. "I just haven't found my rhythm yet," he said.

celtics.headline: Tatum named East Player of the Week
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum won his 14th career Eastern Conference Player of the Week award after averaging 30.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 7 assists in a 4-0 week, including a career-high 22 free-throw attempts and a buzzer-beater against Brooklyn.

bruins.headline: Hagens leaves after Girard cross-check
bruins.summary: Rookie James Hagens left early in the third period of Thursday's win after Samuel Girard cross-checked him in the lower back, and did not return. "I didn't have a chance to see him. Hopefully he will be OK," Marco Sturm said. The Bruins are off Friday and practice Saturday.

bruins.headline: Ten of the next 11 at TD Garden
bruins.summary: Boston opens a four-game homestand Sunday against Florida, followed by Montreal, Minnesota and Los Angeles. The Bruins play 10 of their next 11 games at home and have won 10 of their last 13.

bruins.headline: Best at 5-on-5 in the NHL
bruins.summary: All six goals in Pittsburgh came at even strength, a season high, and Boston is plus-22 at 5-on-5, the league's best. "Every line can score and every line can be out there in any time of the game," Sturm said.

bruins.headline: Bergeron's Hall of Fame weekend; Marchand writes tribute
bruins.summary: Patrice Bergeron is inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame this weekend, and Brad Marchand wrote a testimonial for NHL.com on their years together in Boston.

bruins.headline: Brunet returns with an assist
bruins.summary: Frederic Brunet returned after three straight healthy scratches and assisted on Mark Kastelic's goal. Sturm called the benching a reset, not a punishment.

bruins.headline: Geekie scores in three straight
bruins.summary: Morgan Geekie, who had one goal in his first 14 games, has now scored in three straight. He has had five or more shot attempts in four of the last five games after doing it twice in the first 12. "There's not really any difference between the four lines," he said.

bruins.headline: Lindholm on his best pace since 2021-22
bruins.summary: Elias Lindholm has 14 points in 17 games, a 0.82 points-per-game pace that is his best since his 82-point season with Calgary. He is tied with Hagens for second on the team with six goals, behind David Pastrnak's eight.

bruins.headline: DiPietro improves to 4-1-0
bruins.summary: Michael DiPietro stopped 16 of 18 shots in Pittsburgh to improve to 4-1-0 this season.

bruins.headline: Poitras broke his nose, travels to Pittsburgh
bruins.summary: Matt Poitras broke his nose on Braeden Bowman's elbow Monday and had it reset Tuesday. He practiced Wednesday as a spare forward in a full bubble shield and travels with the team. "We will see how it is tomorrow, and we will go from there," Marco Sturm said.

bruins.headline: Pastrnak passes Bergeron for third on Bruins' goals list
bruins.summary: David Pastrnak's first-period breakaway goal Saturday was his 428th, moving him past former linemate Patrice Bergeron for third in franchise history. "That is a huge milestone and doing that with one franchise, especially with the Boston Bruins, is pretty amazing," Marco Sturm said.

patriots.headline: Henderson reveals hospitalization for neurological symptoms
patriots.summary: TreVeyon Henderson said on Instagram that unexplained neurological symptoms put him in the hospital for several days and have affected his strength and coordination. Testing was reassuring but the cause is unknown; there is no timetable for his return.

patriots.headline: Brown, Henderson out; Henry among seven questionable
patriots.summary: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) will miss a second straight game and Henderson (illness) is out vs. Green Bay. Hunter Henry (foot) returned to limited practice Friday and is questionable, along with Kevin Byard, Carlton Davis, Mack Hollins, Morgan Moses, Brenden Schooler and Greg Van Roten.

patriots.headline: Hollins, Van Roten activation deadline Saturday
patriots.summary: Hollins and Van Roten have 21-day practice windows open and must be activated from injured reserve by 4 p.m. Saturday to play Sunday. Marcus Jones, Dre'Mont Jones and Gabe Jacas came off the injury report.

patriots.headline: Gronkowski enters Patriots Hall of Fame Saturday
patriots.summary: Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction is Saturday at 1 p.m., and Tom Brady will be at Sunday's game.

patriots.headline: Marcus Bryant activated; Vildor released
patriots.summary: The Patriots activated tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve, where he had been since Aug. 30, and released cornerback Kindle Vildor. They also signed linebacker Elias Neal to the practice squad and released WR Cameron Dorner and OL Jake Kubas from it.

patriots.headline: Trade deadline is Nov. 10
patriots.summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. Asked about trade talks, Vrabel said there are "lots of conversations" and "we'll try to do what we can to make the team better."

patriots.headline: Vrabel: no expectations yet on Henry
patriots.summary: Mike Vrabel said Monday he doesn't "have any expectations yet" for Hunter Henry, who left Sunday's game with a foot injury. Mack Hollins and Reggie Gilliam could return this week as they work through the return-to-play process.

patriots.headline: Edge depth thins with Jones also hurt
patriots.summary: Dre'Mont Jones also went down Sunday, leaving Elijah Ponder as the only healthy player the Patriots list at outside linebacker. "It's always tough losing Hunt," Drake Maye said of Henry, adding that he "seems fine in here."

patriots.headline: Vrabel backs Borregales after another miss
patriots.summary: After Andy Borregales's third miss from 40 yards or less this season, Vrabel said "I've got a lot of confidence in Andy" but added, "We have to make our kicks."

patriots.headline: Season-high five sacks, Byard's first Patriots pick
patriots.summary: New England sacked Malik Willis five times, its most this season, led by Cory Durden and Gabe Jacas with 1.5 each. Kevin Byard's interception, his first as a Patriot, set up the clinching touchdown, and Miami ran for 74 yards.

redsox.headline: Contreras, Abreu named Silver Slugger finalists
redsox.summary: Willson Contreras is an American League finalist at first base and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. The two combined for 51 home runs and were Boston's top two in homers and RBIs. Winners are announced Nov. 17.

redsox.headline: Breslow: Red Sox 'operating under the status quo'
redsox.summary: Ahead of the GM meetings in Las Vegas, Craig Breslow said the lockout uncertainty won't change Boston's approach. The bullpen is coming back intact, and he named more offense and pitching depth as priorities.

redsox.headline: Red Sox add Shelley Duncan to coaching staff
redsox.summary: Boston hired Shelley Duncan, who managed the Yankees' Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre affiliate and was the 2025 International League Manager of the Year. His role isn't set; the Red Sox have openings at first- and third-base coach.

redsox.headline: Rafaela, Abreu, Durbin win Gold Gloves
redsox.summary: Ceddanne Rafaela won his second straight Gold Glove in center field and Wilyer Abreu his third straight in right, and Caleb Durbin became the first Red Sox infielder to win one since Ian Kinsler in 2018. It's the first time since 2018 that three Red Sox have won Gold Gloves.

redsox.headline: Red Sox designate Zack Kelly, Eduardo Rivera
redsox.summary: Boston designated right-hander Zack Kelly and left-hander Eduardo Rivera for assignment Monday to meet the deadline for reinstating players from the 60-day IL. Kelly, 31, has a 4.04 ERA in 115 games over five seasons; Rivera, 23, had a 2.96 ERA at Triple-A Worcester. The club has seven days to trade, release or waive them.

redsox.headline: No qualifying offers from Boston
redsox.summary: The Red Sox issued no qualifying offers before Monday's deadline. Sonny Gray was ineligible because he had rejected one with the Twins in 2023. Rule 5 protection decisions are due Nov. 17 and non-tenders Nov. 20.

redsox.headline: Antonio Anderson named AFL Fall-Star
redsox.summary: Infield prospect Antonio Anderson was picked for the American League team in the Arizona Fall League's Fall-Star Game and invited to its Home Run Derby. He is hitting .361 with a 1.123 OPS, 3 homers and 20 RBIs in 16 games for Mesa.

redsox.headline: Red Sox exercise Whitlock's $8.25 million option
redsox.summary: Boston picked up Garrett Whitlock's 2027 club option instead of a $1 million buyout. He had a 1.72 ERA in 54 appearances with 26 holds and pitched through a fractured tibia over the final month; no surgery was needed and he's expected to be ready for spring training.

redsox.headline: Sonny Gray headed to free agency
redsox.summary: Sonny Gray's mutual option for 2027 was declined, triggering a $10 million buyout instead of the $30 million option, and sending the 36-year-old right-hander toward free agency. He posted a 2.72 ERA in 29 starts for Boston this season; the Red Sox can negotiate exclusively with him until Monday.

redsox.headline: Halligan, Bastardo sign minor league deals
redsox.summary: Right-handers Patrick Halligan and Angel Bastardo signed minor league contracts for 2027. Bastardo had a 4.64 ERA with 73 strikeouts in 40 relief appearances at Worcester and is Rule 5-eligible in December.

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
